text:
maria: Quick follow-up to the iterator/routing RFC — a lot of teams are hitting friction when combining prefetch + debounce + transport fallback (grpc -> http/1). We should decide whether the SDK surface exposes prefetch knobs or keeps it opaque to the runtime.
omar: tiny typo: you mean @owen? :)
owen: yes, me. Short answer: expose minimal knobs (target_concurrency, max_prefetch_bytes) and keep debounce/backoff policy as an opaque policy object with a sensible default. Reason: most apps only need a couple of levers; exposing everything invites misuse.
sophie: Agreed on minimal knobs, but we need language parity. Python/TS/Go SDKs should have the same mental model even if names differ. e.g., `prefetch(window)` in TS, `prefetch(max_items=...)` in Python, and a builder in Go.
ryan: Concern: opaque debounce/backoff makes it hard for platform teams to enforce SLAs. We could expose a `policy` interface that teams can implement in enterprise builds. Default remains opaque but pluggable.
maria: That seems reasonable. Proposed surface: top-level options: `prefetch`, `target_concurrency`, `transport_preference` (array: ["grpc","http2","http1"]). Then `policy_factory` optional for advanced users.
owen: Ergonomics notes: in TS we should avoid passing raw async iterators into transport so we can instrument resume tokens for retries. Suggest API: `client.list(...)` returns an `SdkIterator` with `.next()` + `.resume()` token access. Keep streaming and paging consistent across languages.
sophie: For Go we discussed returning a channel vs an iterator type. I still prefer explicit `Iterator.Next(ctx) (Item, Err)` with `Iterator.ResumeToken() string` — easier to port across transports.
ryan: Retry semantics: streaming vs paged. If we prefetch across pages, a failure mid-prefetch should either (A) surface partial results + an error, or (B) retry transparently but must preserve de-dup semantics. I vote for B with idempotency checks and a bounded retry budget per-session.
maria: B with budget sounds right. Document decisions: bounded retry budget, resume token per page, runtime enforces dedupe by request ID and sequence numbers. We'll also provide `on_partial_error` hook for apps that want early visibility.
owen: Transport fallback: prefer policy that fails fast to next transport on AUTH/UNAVAILABLE. Runtime should translate transport error sets to a canonical error code so SDK surface can decide whether to retry or fallback.
ryan: Also add telemetry: emit `prefetch.window_used`, `retry.attempts`, `fallback.triggered` as counters. Helps platform teams tune.
sophie: Action items: (1) Draft TS/py/go surface signatures (2) Add `policy_factory` interface doc + example (3) Implement canonical transport error mapping in runtime.
maria: I'll put a short PR with prototypes for TS and Python surfaces. @owen can you sketch the Go builder?
owen: Yep, I'll drop a sketch later today.
infra-bot: Deploy-check: none needed; design thread only. :white_check_mark: 
maria: Thanks all — keeping the surface minimal + pluggable seems like a good balance. We'll capture the bounded-retry and resume-token invariants in the RFC follow-up.
